title: SB1264 (2018 Regular): Primary and Secondary Schools - Law Enforcement Presence (School Safety Act 2018: Deterrence)

other_topics: education-school-police: Section 1 (Education § 7-441) — police officers placed in public schools, with screening, patrol and student-interaction duties
public-safety-approach: Section 1 (Public Safety § 3-520) — local police and schools set emergency response times

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2018RS/bills/sb/sb1264f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader: the bill as filed. No passage vote recorded. Borderline gun_policy call: the bill is mainly school-police staffing; the gun part is that the officers must carry firearms ('ARMED SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICER' is defined as an officer who carries a firearm). Sub-subsection (C)(2)(II) also says the assigned State Police officer shall carry a firearm.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Education § 7-441): (B) EACH PUBLIC SCHOOL SHALL HAVE AN ARMED SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICER PRESENT ON SCHOOL GROUNDS DURING REGULAR SCHOOL HOURS ON SCHOOL DAYS.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Education § 7-441): (C) (1) IF A PUBLIC SCHOOL IS UNABLE TO MEET THE REQUIREMENT UNDER SUBSECTION (B) OF THIS SECTION, THE DEPARTMENT OF STATE POLICE SHALL ASSIGN A STATE POLICE OFFICER TO THE PUBLIC SCHOOL.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Education § 7-441): (F) A PRIVATE SCHOOL MAY HAVE AN ARMED SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICER PRESENT ON SCHOOL GROUNDS.
